subject: Burst surge orchestration and customer bridge
messages:
From: Elena Voss <elena@fluxly.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: devops@fluxly.com
Date: 2028-07-29 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden request burst causing 10-15s tail latency

Marcus --

We're seeing a sudden surge from our prod traffic starting ~07:45 PST. P95 is up to ~8s and p99s at 12-15s for generation requests. This is affecting checkout chat suggestions (critical path). We already throttled our client side to 30rps but backend p99s keep spiking.

Attached is a short sample of logs and a few request IDs. Can Redwood help escalate and open a bridge? We're on a tight release and need something stable in the next 3 hours.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Voss
Head of Platform Reliability, Fluxly
(elena@fluxly.com)

Attachments: fluxly_log_snippet.txt (text), recent-req-ids.txt (text)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Elena Voss <elena@fluxly.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden request burst causing 10-15s tail latency

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and the logs. We'll open a bridge and start triage ASAP. Proposed immediate plan: 
1) 08:30 PDT bridge (15 min) to share traces and decide mitigations.
2) Ben/infra to validate if KV cache hit-rate or batching is degrading.
3) Quick product toggle options (grace) — reduce model max tokens / enable conservative caching.
4) If needed, temporary routing to a smaller-capacity but lower-latency model variant as fallback.

I'll kick off the bridge invite and attach a short log from our side. Please add any other SREs.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden request burst causing 10-15s tail latency

Adding initial observations from infra:
- We're seeing an abnormal growth in KV cache evictions over the last 30m correlating with Fluxly request IDs (trace ids attached to internal trace).
- GPU queue depth on a subset of nodes hit sustained 75-80% for long seq requests ( > 700 tokens) which amplifies tail.
- No obvious host failures or OOMs; network metrics look normal.

Immediate actions I can take during bridge:
- Force eviction of stale models from a small pool to free KV capacity (minute-level action).
- Flip a temporary batching cap so long sequences don't crowd short requests.

I'll prepare a small log bundle for the bridge (attaching fluxly-related snippet).

-ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_fluxly_trace_bundle.log

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden request burst causing 10-15s tail latency

High-level product asks / quick toggles I want to evaluate on the bridge: 
- Reduce default max_tokens for gen requests sent by Fluxly's API key (non-breaking, lowers mean compute).
- Enable conservative kv_cache TTL for Fluxly traffic group for 30m (if accurate hits are low it reduces churn).
- Short-term model variant fallback: route to lower-latency quantized variant for checkout path only.

We should also capture: what quality delta they'd accept and how to revert quickly.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Product — Serving & Reliability
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden request burst causing 10-15s tail latency

Operational notes from infra-engineering: 
- We can push two quick changes with low risk: 1) impose per-key max_seq cap (ceiling on token count) at the routing layer, 2) temporarily lower batching depth for requests coming from the Fluxly tenant. Both are feature flags with immediate rollback.
- I'll stage the route-change in canary and be ready to flip during the bridge. Expect ~90s to fully propagate.

I'll be on the bridge and will maintain the rollback playbook in chat.

—Mina
